page: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is an entry-level virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 1 vCPU consisting of 1 physical core and 1 thread, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is provided by a bundled 30 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server.

Benchmark results highlight a distinct contrast between single-core processing capabilities and overall system throughput. The dedicated AMD EPYC core delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25%. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with read-only large block transfers at 31.44 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 22.58 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, perform at average levels. Conversely, database operations, Redis SET operations at 2.3 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 1.61 GB/sec rank in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated AMD EPYC resources, making it accessible for workloads that do not require massive parallel processing or high memory bandwidth. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent single-threaded performance without the noisy-neighbor issues of shared-core environments. This server is recommended for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development environments, simple automation scripts, and low-traffic applications that benefit from dedicated CPU execution but have modest memory and storage requirements.
